messages:
maria: Quick sync — we need a final recommendation for Dedicated pool sizing for the new 65B quant bring-up. Goal: p99 <= 220ms for chat-style 512-token tails, steady-state throughput target ~120 RPS per slab. Region split: us-west primary, eu-west fallback. Any packing/concurrency proposals?

devin: baseline numbers from last week's runs: h100 80GB with q4f16 gave p50~45ms, p99~210ms at concurrency 8 per GPU (batching enabled). a100 80GB is ~25% slower at p99 under same concurrency.

sam: are these runs single-tenant slabs? numbers matter for autoscale headroom. also: tail behavior during cold KV-cache misses was ~+60ms.

maria: yes single-tenant. we expect multi-tenant packing for cost-efficiency though — want to keep per-tenant concurrency cap. proposal: target concurrency 6 per GPU for multi-tenant steady state, allow short bursts to 10 with autoscale buffer. thoughts?

ryan: sounds reasonable. simulation shows concurrency=6 gives p99~180ms on h100 with our batching heuristics. but in eu-west latency rises ~15-25ms due to network and kernel differences. so we need region-specific headroom.

kim: +1. also quant kernel choice matters: truncated-attn kernel reduces memory pressure but adds ~5-10ms on h100 for long context. q4f16 vs q5_1 tradeoffs discussed earlier. which quant config are we pinning?

maria: for initial rollout use q4f16 (verified by eng-ml). can we run a sweep: (h100,a100) x (concurrency 4,6,8) x (q4f16,q5_1) across us-west/eu-west and capture p50/p95/p99 and throughput? include cold-warm KV cache scenarios.

sam: I'll schedule the sweep. quick note on packing: if we allow tenant packing factor 1.5 (i.e., avg 50% slot sharing), effective concurrency per physical GPU rises — we should lower per-tenant cap to keep p99 SLOs.

devin: Agree. Numeric example in sim: physical GPU with concurrency=6, packing factor 1.5 -> effective 9. p99 on h100 at effective 9 jumps to ~240ms. so set tenant cap to 5 to keep headroom for bursts and autoscale.

alexa: deploy-bot: scheduled perf-sweep job 3198768000, logs -> s3://redwood-perf/65b/3198768000/ (ETA 3h) :robot_face:

maria: good. ops question: what's our autoscale policy recommendation? immediate scale for 15% sustained queue depth for 2 minutes? or scale more aggressively for short microbursts?

ryan: we use slot-based autoscale. suggestion: maintain a 20% spare GPU headroom in us-west under normal load to cover regional jitter and kernel variance. allow rapid ephemeral burst slots via pre-warmed buffer for 60s. that maps to reserved 1.2x capacity in autoscale sim.

kim: we should differentiate headroom by model family. 65B quant tail latency more sensitive, so +25% buffer for those pools. smaller models can keep 15%.

sam: adding a note: warmup cost (KV-cache fill) for cold starts is ~0.3s per request for long tails — we should prefer warm slab reuse for canary traffic. will add to runbook.

devin: also include fallback policy: on sustained p99 > 240ms, fallback route to a slightly smaller model variant (50B or reduced context) to preserve latency SLOs while autoscale catches up. ops: is that acceptable?

maria: yes, fallback to 50B-quant variant is our plan. add a metric-based rollback if quality regression exceeds threshold.

alexa: deploy-bot: perf-sweep job completed 3198771600, summary report -> https://dash.redwood.internal/perf/65b/3198768000 :white_check_mark:

sam: quick summary from sweep: h100 q4f16 @ concurrency 6 -> p99 us-west 190ms, eu-west 210ms. h100 concurrency 8 -> p99 us-west 230ms. a100 q4f16 concurrency 6 -> p99 us-west 235ms. q5_1 increases p99 by ~12-18ms across configs. cold KV cache added ~55-70ms on p99. throughput numbers match targets only on h100 concurrency 6+.

ryan: so recommended default pool: h100 80GB, per-GPU concurrency cap 6, tenant cap 5, reserved headroom 25% for 65B-quant pools in us-west, 30% in eu-west. autoscale policy: scale at 2m sustained 70% slot utilization, pre-warm buffer 1 extra GPU for 60s.

maria: that reads well. I'll draft the proposal for payment/accounting: estimate cost delta from reserved headroom and multi-region redundancy.

devin: one more thing — kernel selection: prefer faster attention kernels for p99-critical paths even if they slightly raise memory usage. add a flag in runtime to prefer p99-optimized kernels for Dedicated SLA pools.

maria: agreed. action items: sam -> add runbook entries + canary playbook (due EOD), devin -> open runtime flag PR for kernel preference, ryan -> update autoscale sims with 25/30% headroom delta, kim -> finalize quant config doc. I'll circulate the draft to eng-ops and product. :thumbsup:

alexa: deploy-bot: action items tracked in ticket RD-INF-7243.

maria: thanks everyone. we'll reconvene after canary results.
